newsitem.title: FINLAND: Amer battered to 8-month loss by sports.
newsitem.headline: Amer battered to 8-month loss by sports.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer, dogged by weak sales in golf, tennis and ski equipment, said Thursday it had fallen deeply into the red in the January-August period and would continue to lose money this year.

Amer, whose Wilson tennis rackets are used by top professionals including Pete Sampras and Steffi Graf, swung to a January-August loss of 206 million markka ($45.1 million) from a 36 million markka ($7.8 million) profit before extraordinary items a year earlier.
In a statement, Amer repeated a warning that it will remain "clearly loss-making" this year. Last year it booked a 142 million markka ($31 million) profit before extras and tax.
Amer said its net sales, which fell 24 percent to 3.22 billion markka ($700 million), would continue to shrink.
Amer said it expected losses from all three of its big-brand sports units, Wilson, MacGregor and Atomic, which together made up 76 percent of January-August net sales.
Problems at Wilson were mainly due to continued difficulties in golf club and ball sales, as well as lower sales and profitability in clothing and baseball products, Amer said.
But Amer said Wilson would remain in all its current product areas. "Wilson is maintaining its strong market position in all team sports product categories in the U.S.," Amer said.
While MacGregor Golf Company sales had been above target in the Asia-Pacific region, Amer said they fell short of expectations in the United States and Europe.
